SearchAliases: two halls fight over a cat
Nanquan cuts the cat in two
Senses.Explanation: Nanquan's public cat-cutting case, not a general instruction to cut a cat. This graph form occurs 156 times in 53 allowlisted texts and names the same event as the alternative cat graph. The east and west halls fight over a cat; Nanquan holds it up and says that an answer will spare it; the assembly gives no answer and he cuts it in two. When Zhaozhou returns, he puts a sandal on his head and leaves; Nanquan says that his presence would have saved the cat. Later records make the phrase a case title, a public question, a verse subject, and a cited precedent. A question explicitly invokes the major precept against killing and asks why Nanquan cut the cat and Guizong cut the snake; Miyun Yuanwu tells the questioner to repent. Dahui Zonggao reports that students call the two cases ‘timely wondrous function’ or ‘great function appearing without retaining rules,’ then rejects both accounts. The entry preserves the hard precept question and Dahui's rejection without inventing a rationale for the killing.
Senses.Note: The two written cat forms are searchable family members but name one event. The full event without the contiguous headword is family evidence; six exact witnesses across six sources clear the floor. Case title, verse, and later question are deployments of the same event, not separate things. The precept-violation dispute is reported without ruling whether the act is justified.

Occurrences.Kwic: 南泉一日。東西兩堂爭猫兒南泉見遂提起云。道得即不斬眾無對泉斬却猫兒為兩段泉復舉前話問趙州州便脫草鞋。於頭上戴出泉云。子若在。恰救得猫兒。

Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps, volumes 10–25 (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), within Miyun Yuanwu's section, an unnamed monk asks the exact public precept question joining Nanquan's cat-cutting and Guizong's snake-cutting; Miyun answers by telling the questioner to repent.
